sentences.text:
And And Another Counsel for Applicant :- Ajay Pratap Singh,Naresh Kumar Pathak Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Suresh Kumar Gupta,J.
Vakalatnama filed by Mr. Raj Priya Srivastava, Advocate on behalf of the opposite party no.2 is taken on record.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material available on record.

This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant for quashing the summoning order dated 1.10.2021 as well as the entire proceedings of Complaint Case No. 59912 of 2021, under Sections 138 N.I. Act, Police Station- Gosaiganj, District- Lucknow.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the agreement to sale was entered on 27.2.2016 between the son of the opposite party no.2 Ahishek and the applicant for purchasing the land measuring 1600 sq. feet situated at Mohanlalganj regarding which Rs. 4,50,000/- was given to the son of the opposite party no.2 as a premium payment but the sale deed could not execute between the parties.

It is further submitted that meanwhile son of the opposite party no.2 executed sale deed Shiv Bahadur vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Home Civil ... on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112335842/
1 in favour of his mother and not executed in favour of the applicant and thus, the FIR was lodged by the applicant against the opposite party no.2 and her son on 7.11.2020 as a case crime No.
554/2020, U/s 419,420,467,4648,504,506 IPC.

sentences.text: Ultimately, the opposite party no.2 agreed to execute the sale deed in favour of the applicant for the said land and as such, sale deed was executed by the opposite party no.2 regarding which Rs. 4,50,000/- was transferred in account of opposite party no.2 after execution of sale deed through NEFT/RTGS and at the time of sale deed, two cheques bearing Nos. 671197 and 671198 were given to her in good faith with stipulated condition that both the cheques would be returned by the opposite party no.2.
But the opposite party no.2 only returned the cheque No. 671197.
The applicant transferred the money in the account of opposite party no.2 in two different ways i.e. Rs. 2 lakhs on 14.6.2021 through RTGS and Rs. 2.5 lakhs on 12.7.2021 through NEFT.

But the aforesaid blank cheque No. 671198 was not returned by the opposite party no.2 and she filled the amount of Rs. 8,10,000/- therein and presented in the bank but the same was dishonoured and thus, the false and frivolous complaint case U/s 138 N.I. Act has been filed against the applicant in which he was summoned to face trial.

Learned A.G.A. as well as the counsel for the complainant vehemently opposes the submissions advanced by the counsel for the applicant and submits that the aforesaid cheques were given in lieu of sale deed which is not fully described in sale deed and this is the admitted fact that the said cheques were issued by the applicant.

So far as quashing of entire proceedings is concerned, from the perusal of the material on record and looking into the facts of the case at this stage, it cannot be said that no offence is made out against the petitioners.
All the submission made relates to the disputed question of fact, which cannot be adjudicated upon by this Court.

At this stage, only prima facie case is to be seen in the light of the law laid down by Supreme Court in cases of R.P. Kapur Vs. State of Punjab, A.I.R. 1960 S.C. 866, State of Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal, 1992 SCC (Cr.) 426, State of Bihar Vs. P.P.Sharma, 1992 SCC (Cr.) 192 and lastly Zandu Pharmaceutical Works Ltd. Vs. Mohd. Saraful Haq and another (Para-10) 2005 SCC (Cr.) 283.

sentences.text: The disputed defence of the accused cannot be considered at this stage.

Moreover, the petitioner has got a right of discharge according to the provisions prescribed in Cr.P.C., as the case may be, through a proper application for the said purpose and he is free to take all the submissions in the said discharge application before the trial court.

So far as the summoning order passed by the learned trial court is concerned, at the stage of taking cognizance, trial court can simply form an opinion as to whether the case is fit for taking and committing the matter for trial or not.
In the present case, learned trial court clearly expressed his opinion that he perused all the record and clearly indicated that the material placed before him is sufficient to proceed the case.
Thus, the cognizance order is not a proforma order.
Every aspect is touched by learned trial court and petitioner failed to adduce any evidence which caused prejudiced to him.
So, the cognizance and summoning order is perfectly valid and there is no occasion to quash the same.
The prayer for quashing the impugned proceedings as well as impugned summoning order is refused.
